<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Typed link relations: semantics on the rel, not the field name; five built-ins frozen (pressure, proven_by, satisfies, derives, ref); unknown rels legal as ref.
- Every list item can carry a links bucket (list-typed rel ref), auto-rendered as a final table column, traversed by dd graph map.
- Every done_when assertion names its instrument: pressure is a BP-row link or the literal not-applicable; absence is a validation ERROR.
- evidence sections become done_when; task rows carry satisfies (always an array) back to the ACs they serve.
- harness plan validate grows the semantic layer: open-completables summary, rel-generic contradiction warnings, --complete mode with strict-zero green, and --address scoping to any proof subgraph.
- The flow gains a check-kind gate: the last review node refuses departure until plan validate --complete is green; phase nodes gate on their task sections; the template/expander author all of it.
- 1b plan and 5 tasks author .dd.json natively; ship renders the dd-derived AC/evidence table into the PR body.
- The dd command surface is taught positionally: baked into node instructions[] and each stage module at its seam.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No probe execution anywhere in dd/plan surfaces — harness checks owns instrument execution (ruled, twice).
- No AC-state derivation — closure stays a performed act; agents close, guard rails make it trustworthy.
- No code-drift freshness beyond the existing basis ledger.
- No migration of existing markdown plans; the archive is institutional memory, not a conversion backlog.
- No per-assertion satisfies (ruled: task row, coarse).
- No allowlist/policy surface for --complete warnings (ruled: strict zero; --force is the bypass).
- No changes to the five lifecycle hooks, the harness-seam doctrine, or the E44x gate-code meanings.
